tldr: On-device and browser-local AI gained notable new tooling: QVAC described a 0.8B assistant, PyTorch added a WebGPU inference path, and TNG explored modular MoE specialization; benchmark performance remains largely author-reported.

Google broadened Gemini 4 Carbon access while a new SVG-animation benchmark showed how executable graders can complement model judgments; Helsing's military-agent platform and renewed US–China AI dialogue warrant scrutiny of safety claims, oversight and real-world evidence.
Three reports are dated November 11 and seven November 10; five technology and three terminology proposals remain deferred, with incomplete source coverage.

news.title: QVAC introduces BotPsy, a sub-billion-parameter tool-use assistant
news.summary: QVAC published BotPsy, an approximately 0.8B-parameter model adapted from Qwen3.5-0.8B for on-device assistants and multi-step tool calls, with a multi-stage training procedure and author-run evaluations.
news.why_it_matters: Specialized small models can offer private, lower-resource tool use, making the approach relevant to local assistants instead of routing every interaction to frontier APIs.
news.caveat: Reported benchmark improvements are author evaluations, not independent replications; the paper acknowledges significant remaining safety weaknesses, including susceptibility to harmful instructions and prompt injection. Actual downloadable checkpoint terms and hardware performance require separate verification.

news.title: Helsing announces Clarity, a military multi-agent intelligence platform
news.summary: Helsing unveiled Clarity, an agent-based platform intended to join sensor streams, reports and other military data into an intelligence picture with human review in the decision workflow.
news.why_it_matters: It illustrates operational deployment ambitions for multi-agent information fusion and raises consequential questions about evidence quality, automation bias and human control in military settings.
news.caveat: Its performance and human-control safeguards are company descriptions; independent field validation and actual deployment coverage were not established. Do not confuse platform marketing with proven operational effectiveness.

news.title: Google expands Gemini 4 Carbon availability and agent tooling
news.summary: Google announced broader access to Gemini 4 Carbon through its developer and customer surfaces and described agent coordination through Antigravity's preview /swarm workflow.
news.why_it_matters: Developers evaluating long-context multimodal models and collaborative coding agents now have a newly described access and workflow option.
news.caveat: Availability, quota and billing vary by product and eligibility; Google benchmarks are vendor-reported and the coordination feature is preview, not a universally released stable API.

news.title: ExecuTorch gains a WebGPU path for local browser inference
news.summary: The PyTorch team documented an ExecuTorch WebGPU backend that runs exported PyTorch models as .pte files on supported browser GPUs, including examples spanning text, vision and speech.
news.why_it_matters: Direct browser-local GPU execution can preserve prompt data on a device and reduce dependency on cloud inference for compatible workloads.
news.caveat: Authors' speed comparisons against their selected CPU path are not cross-framework benchmarks. Model coverage, memory, WebGPU browser support and device-specific compatibility must be tested.

news.title: Figma and Stanford release an SVG animation benchmark with executable checks
news.summary: MotionGraphicsBench introduces 100 static-SVG-to-motion tasks graded with explicit executable verification programs; its researchers evaluated 32 model configurations and released benchmark resources.
news.why_it_matters: Task-specific programmatic graders can complement model-as-judge evaluation when outputs have properties that can be checked deterministically.
news.caveat: Authors report only four evaluated systems exceeded 50% pass@1 and a 93.3% raw grader-human agreement on a held-out sample; results and grader correctness are not independently reproduced, and grading tests can miss visual quality.

news.title: TNG explores adding independently trained specialists to MoE models
news.summary: TNG researchers describe training and integrating new domain-specific experts into an existing mixture-of-experts base model, with worked coding-domain experiments and comparisons against adapter fine-tuning.
news.why_it_matters: Modular domain adaptation could help small teams specialize an MoE model without retraining every existing expert or deploying separate full models.
news.caveat: The authors' evaluations are workload-specific; expert-router compatibility, quality tradeoffs and total memory requirements limit portability, and this is not a universal plug-and-play skill transfer result.

news.title: OpenAI opens beta business listings and scoped Business Agents in ChatGPT
news.summary: OpenAI introduced Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, including business-claimed information, aggregate discovery insights and Business Agents initially offered to eligible U.S. ecommerce and online-service businesses.
news.why_it_matters: The release creates a distinct business-to-user agent interaction surface with implications for discovery, attribution, trust and merchant data maintenance.
news.caveat: This is a restricted beta, not an account-wide public rollout. Availability, eligibility and data practices must be checked against product documentation; no independent outcome metrics were established.

news.title: Anthropic starts roadshow for a proposed public offering
news.summary: Anthropic launched a roadshow for a proposed stock offering with an indicated $70–$78 share-price range and a planned Nasdaq listing under ANT.
news.why_it_matters: A proposed listing could reshape public-market scrutiny of frontier-model economics, capital needs and governance.
news.caveat: This is a proposed, not completed, IPO. The company's statement says the registration statement had not yet become effective, so pricing, timing and completion remain uncertain.

news.title: OpenAI and Upwork report shifting demand for AI-related freelance work
news.summary: An OpenAI–Upwork analysis describes changes in posted freelance tasks, combinations of requested skills and larger project budgets among AI-related work on the platform.
news.why_it_matters: It supplies a concrete platform-level signal about how businesses are restructuring some contracted work around AI.
news.caveat: The sample represents Upwork postings, not the whole labor market; associations cannot establish that AI caused the reported shifts, and the analysis involves the participating companies.

news.title: US and China discuss possible AI incident-alert and testing dialogue
news.summary: Reuters reports that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a clear-eyed approach to AI cooperation and competition and described potential discussions on model testing practices and incident alerts.
news.why_it_matters: Even preliminary international coordination about testing and incident reporting matters for cross-border AI safety governance.
news.caveat: Reported remarks and prospective talks do not constitute a binding agreement, functioning alert channel or adopted regulatory standard.
